clue.text: Taxi's predecessor bans macho capers

indicators.note: capers are frisky leaps, so the letters before it jump about into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply all nine letters

explanation.surface: An old cab driver puts a stop to swaggering behaviour among passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: A HANSOM CAB was the two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of Victorian London, the forerunner of the motor taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn hire carriages plied city streets before motorised cabs replaced them, so they came first historically.

clue.text: Plant one under chap giving party

indicators.note: in a down answer under places the first item below the second, so it comes after it

parts.note: the man throwing a party is its host
a means one

explanation.surface: A man hosting a gathering lays out a single plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are shade-loving perennials grown in gardens for their broad ornamental leaves.

clue.text: Keeping a watchful eye on medical profession

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tending or looking after carefully
second meaning: the job of caring for the sick

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb form it means tending carefully, and as a noun it is the occupation of caring for patients.

clue.text: Unfashionable, more seemly clothes are her stock

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
fitter is the comparative of fit, meaning suitable or proper

explanation.surface: Dowdy but more decent garments are what she keeps in her shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shopkeeper who sells clothing and equipment, so garments are the trade's merchandise.

clue.text: Someone prophesying doom as canards spread

indicators.note: rumours that spread get scattered about, so these letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: all nine letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A doom-monger warns as false rumours circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Cassandra foretold Troy's fall but was fated never to be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: Her name is used for anyone who predicts disaster, usually without being heeded.

clue.text: English county short of American cash

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shortened name of Buckinghamshire, a county west of London

explanation.surface: An English county is running low on US dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' looks like a deletion; 'short' belongs to the first definition, meaning abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated county name equals the US slang plural for dollars.

clue.text: Harness on pony's back is vulgar

parts.note: tack is the saddle, bridle and other gear for a horse

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the animal's name is used

parts.note: the final letter of pony

explanation.surface: Fancy horse gear on a little pony looks cheap and gaudy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky is an informal synonym for cheap, showy and in poor taste.

clue.text: He adjusts barrel with beer half gone

indicators.note: half gone means one of the two halves of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
taken as written before losing its first half

explanation.surface: A man tinkers with a cask whose beer is half drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuner is a person who adjusts instruments such as pianos to the correct pitch.

clue.text: Cooked luncheon loses nothing on way to France

indicators.note: cooked food is altered, so the remaining letters are mixed up
loses tells us to take something away from the meal word

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: A meal cooked for a journey to France is eaten in full.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from LUNCHEON, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chunnel is the nickname for the Channel Tunnel linking England with France under the sea.

clue.text: Now — as of tomorrow, anyway

parts.note: surface reading: the present moment
setter's reading: today, looked back on from tomorrow, is the day before

explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks what today will be called once tomorrow arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: From the standpoint of tomorrow, the present day becomes the day before, which is the word for the previous day.

clue.text: Hint of reduction in rank — it casts a cloud

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the word for rank

parts.note: status is standing or rank

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of reduction

explanation.surface: A demotion casts a gloom over the person who suffers it.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside STATUS after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat, grey layer of cloud, one of the basic cloud types.

clue.text: Briefly knock out blighter behind swindle

indicators.note: behind puts the first word's equivalent after the second's in the finished word

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a cuss is an informal word for a fellow, a blighter

explanation.surface: Someone tells us to knock the rascal behind a fraud senseless for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' looks like an abbreviation signal but belongs to the definition: a concussion knocks someone out for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To concuss is to injure the brain by a blow, typically causing temporary unconsciousness.

clue.text: i Bail out one with evidence she was elsewhere

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman is released on bail because of proof she was not at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray lowercase 'i' at the start of the printed clue is a scanning artefact and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim, with proof, that an accused person was somewhere other than the crime scene.

clue.text: Promise freedom from doubt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pledge or guarantee

explanation.surface: A vow that settles all uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a formal pledge given to someone and the state of being confident and certain.

clue.text: Sound of relief at opening of theatrical spectacle

parts.note: a sigh is the breath let out when relieved

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of theatrical

explanation.surface: A theatregoer exhales gratefully as the grand show finally begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something worth seeing, an impressive display or show, just like a spectacle.

clue.text: Vessel has sides enclosed; it needs boilers

indicators.note: has means the first word holds something, here the word for sides
enclosed confirms the sides sit within the vessel word rather than beside it

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
sides in sport are teams

explanation.surface: A ship with enclosed sides needs boilers to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' suggests a ship's hull, but in sport sides are teams; the last clause defines the whole vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is driven by steam raised in boilers, so these are essential to its propulsion.

clue.text: Resident monk chemical firm guided

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some Benedictine monks
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, the big British chemical company
led means guided

explanation.surface: A monk who lives on site steered a chemicals company.
explanation.definitionFit: Domiciled means having a settled home in a place, as a resident does; the adjective swaps for resident.

clue.text: Wrongly use Military Intelligence's name

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, plus the possessive S
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Spies are accused of abusing their organisation's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle is to deal with something badly or treat it improperly, misusing it.

clue.text: Left in tents depressed by tough restriction

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for tents

parts.note: a camp is a group of tents
L is the abbreviation for left
feeling down is feeling depressed

explanation.surface: Campers left in their tents feel low after strict new rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed by' looks like a container instruction, but it just means the word for depressed follows on.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a severe official crackdown imposing firm restrictions on some activity.

clue.text: Bears arms in scuffle, to cause unease

indicators.note: a scuffle is a confused tussle, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: all nine letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone carrying weapons in a brawl unsettles the onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them feel awkward, self-conscious and uncomfortable.

clue.text: Silly mistake about account for pig

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a blunder wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: a boner is a foolish blunder
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A foolish error in the books is blamed on a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A baconer is a pig reared and fattened specifically to be cured for bacon.

clue.text: Where to change baby outside English church building

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the word's letters are rearranged
outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: the letters of baby, shuffled
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question about where to find a baby-changing room near a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change baby' reads as nappy duty; it is the shuffle, with E then placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a church, often large, attached to or once belonging to a monastery or convent.

clue.text: Pain after centre of suburb is countrified

indicators.note: after places the word for pain behind the selected letters
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the two in the middle

parts.note: the two middle letters of suburb
colic is a severe stomach pain

explanation.surface: Suburban life is a pain, and the suburb is going rural.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes pastoral, rustic country life, so it suits countrified in sense and part of speech.

clue.text: Tarred surface, one in front of a nut-tree

indicators.note: in front of puts the road-surface word before the pieces that follow it

parts.note: macadam is road surfacing of broken stone, often bound with tar
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road surface laid in front of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian evergreen tree grown for its rich, round edible nuts.

clue.text: Attractive bit of ground is hypermarket's choice

indicators.note: a bit of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them
choice suggests a selection picked out of the text in front of it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of ground through is into the start of hypermarket's

explanation.surface: A supermarket picks an appealing plot of land for its new store.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishy is British slang for good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is an informal word for sexually attractive, so it replaces the adjective directly.

clue.text: Touch of lime in a great deal of soil covering

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the phrase for a lot

parts.note: much means a great deal

indicators.note: a touch is a tiny amount, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of lime

explanation.surface: A gardener adds a little lime to a large amount of topsoil dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulch is a layer of compost, bark or similar spread over soil to protect it and retain moisture.

clue.text: Speeds shown to demonstrate one's ability

definitions.meaning: second meaning: as in being put through them to show what one can do

explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the idiom 'put through one's paces', where a horse or person is tested.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means rates of going, and in the idiom it names the routines displayed to prove capability.

clue.text: Sad or rueful, recalling youthful beginnings

definitions.text: Sad or rueful, recalling youthful beginnings

indicators.note: beginnings are the starts of words, so the first letter of each is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone feels wistful and regretful looking back on their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: being sad and rueful when remembering early days.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry means feeling regret or sorrow, exactly the mood of sad, rueful reminiscence.

clue.text: Gift wrapped in old cloth and Sellotape

indicators.note: wrapped in says the wanted word sits inside the following words, covered by them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cloth, all of and, and the start of Sellotape

explanation.surface: A present wrapped up in old fabric and sticky tape.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDSEL is an old word, mainly Scottish, for a gift marking a new year or new venture; 'old' in the surface hints at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is a traditional present given for good luck at a beginning, such as New Year.

clue.text: Odd lore interpreted by one drawing idly

indicators.note: to interpret is to render in another form, so the letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Strange folklore explained by an idle sketcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodler is someone who scribbles aimless little pictures while their mind is elsewhere.

clue.text: Deflect growing salmon to source of Yarrow

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of Yarrow

explanation.surface: Steer a young salmon towards the head of the Yarrow, a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry is to ward off or turn aside a blow or an awkward question.

clue.text: Cut, you could say, and greet noisy pursuers

indicators.note: you could say means as spoken, so the word is matched by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to hew is to cut, and it is pronounced like hue
taken as written
greet is Scots for weep or cry

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a figure and welcomes a rowdy crowd giving chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greet' looks like welcome, but in Scots it means to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry was the old public outcry raised by people chasing a criminal; now any loud clamour.
